Re100 lid-driven cavity: Ghia centerline comparison March a real nonperiodic 2D viscous incompressible solver to steady state on 17/33/65 node grids and compare against original Ghia centerlines. Retain streamlines, grid vortex center, true PDE residual and discrete divergence. Input and validation protocol history · Initial input Assumptions, units and boundaries Dimensionless unit square, viscosity .01, lid speed1, Re=100. Top interior nodes have u=1; other walls and all four corners have zero velocity. Psi=0 on every wall; initial interior vorticity 0. Reapply Thom wall vorticity at every Heun stage. Editorial clarification Educational Re=100 checks on three fixed grids. Lid/sidewall corner velocities are discontinuous; stationary corners take precedence. Ghia values are rounded numerical references, not an exact solution, and printed four-decimal coordinates are preserved. No high-Re, turbulence, original-algorithm reproduction or cavity-pressure validation is claimed. Scientific-source revision3, immutable edition2026-11-23-r2, passed22 unit checks and all94 group gates. After the initial NumPy-boolean JSON-serialization failure, the next unpublished candidate lacked completion status and case-ID top-level checks required by the common verifier. This edition only repairs the JSON envelope with termination,failure and case-keyed checks, retaining the prior three diagnostics under summary_checks, and adds one regression. Inputs,acceptance,numerical solver,references and the prior21 tests are unchanged. All six saved NPZ field arrays are bit-identical to the previous candidate. The original unpublished packet is archived outside the public tree, and earlier failure history is retained. Finest Ghia centerline maximum errors are about.00277820 foru and.00590408 forv; the grid primary vortex is(.609375,.734375), with true steady residual about9.68e-10. Pressure is eliminated in streamfunction evolution; cavity pressure is not validated. Adopted numerical method Advance vorticity transport with centered differences and Heun. Each stage solves−Delta_h psi=omega using a nonperiodic Dirichlet DST, then forms u=psi_y,v=−psi_x.
